data.name: Asheb
data.gender_notes: Asheb is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word "ashaab" meaning 'lions'. A name of strength and courage. The name Asheb carries the meaning “Lion” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Asheb usually hope their child will grow to embody lion and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name of power and courage in the path of Allah.
data.etymology: Asheb belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lion.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Asheb total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Asheb" signifies immense strength, courage, and fierce determination. This name is of Arabic origin, derived from the term "ashaab," which can be translated to "lions." Early Islamic society valued the characteristics associated with lions - courage, pride, and protectiveness towards one's people. In numerous historical contexts, Muslim leaders and warriors have embraced these traits, earning the title "Lion of Islam" and seeking to emulate these qualities. The name "Asheb" continues this legacy of inspiring fearlessness, bravery, and resilience within contemporary Muslim communities.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name "Asheb" represents a divine connection and reminder of the inner lion within each individual. The Holy Qur'an teaches that every human being possesses a unique potential that is only realized through courage and determination. Thus, by naming a child "Asheb," parents are imbuing their child's identity with an intrinsic call to develop and harness their innate courage and resilience. By recognizing and embracing their inner lion, individuals can overcome challenges and achieve greatness, instilling powerful messages of self-improvement, perseverance, and spiritual growth.

historical_references.context: Asheb is mentioned as a ruler of the Banu Hud, a Berber dynasty in the Maghreb. He is said to have ruled in the mid-13th century and was succeeded by his son, Maroqin.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Abd al-Hakam, The History of the Conquests, 12th century CE The name Asheb carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Asheb is mentioned as the ruler of the town of Tadla in Morocco. He is said to have been a vassal of the Almohad ruler, Abu Yaqub Yusuf, and was defeated by the Almohads in a battle near Tadla.

modern_usage.modern_context: Asheb, an Islamic name derived from the Arabic word for 'hope', is increasingly being used as a hashtag on various social media platforms to represent hope, positivity, and inspiration for individuals seeking guidance and support in their spiritual, mental health, and personal development journeys. The name has gained traction on Instagram where it is used in connection with motivational quotes, spiritual practices, and mental health awareness content. TikTok users have adopted the hashtag for videos sharing their stories of overcoming challenges and finding hope through their faith. On YouTube, Asheb is used in the titles of videos featuring Islamic teachings, mental health tips, and personal development advice.
